sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: In the shadow of Silicon Valley, San Francisco is home to a futuristic eatery with a virtual cashier putting change on the menu.
sentences.zh: 在硅谷的阴影下，旧金山有一家充满未来感的餐馆，它用虚拟收银员把找零也变成了菜单的一部分。

sentences.en: There was a new restaurant that opened a few years back in downtown San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 几年前，旧金山市中心开了一家新餐馆。

sentences.en: It was called Itza.
sentences.zh: 它叫Itza。

sentences.en: Itza, a high-tech new restaurant where you order on iPads and get your quinoa bowls out of a cubby.
sentences.zh: Itza是一家高科技新餐馆，你可以在iPad上点餐，然后从储物格里取出你的藜麦碗。

sentences.en: And instead of placing an order with a waiter or someone behind the counter, you punch in your order on a screen.
sentences.zh: 你不需要和侍者或柜台后面的人点餐，而是直接在屏幕上输入你的订单。

sentences.en: It's terrific for those of us who are antisocial.
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些有社交恐惧的人来说，这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: You don't have to actually talk to a person.
sentences.zh: 你根本不需要和人说话。

sentences.en: Just swipe your card.
sentences.zh: 刷一下卡就行了。

sentences.en: And then a few minutes later, you would walk to a wall of clear glass cubbies.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，你走到一堵透明玻璃储物格墙前。

sentences.en: It'll go dark for just a second so you don't see the actual food being placed in the cubby.
sentences.zh: 它会变暗一秒钟，这样你就看不到食物被放进格子的过程。

sentences.en: And then when the food was placed, the cubby would glow with your name.
sentences.zh: 当食物放好后，储物格就会亮起你的名字。

sentences.en: You'd tap the glass twice and you could open the cubby and your food order was in there waiting for you.
sentences.zh: 你敲两下玻璃，就能打开格子，取走为你准备好的餐点。

sentences.en: You tap it, you get your food and you leave.
sentences.zh: 敲一下，取餐，然后离开。

sentences.en: The fact that you can just order on the iPad, pick it out of the cubby and go back to your desk means it's really about the most productive way you can get lunch.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接在iPad上点餐，从格子里取餐，然后回到办公桌，这意味着这是你能享用午餐最高效的方式。

sentences.en: You never had to interact with a single person if you didn't want to.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想，你完全不需要和任何人交流。

sentences.en: You didn't have to tip.
sentences.zh: 你也不需要付小费。

sentences.en: It was faSt.
sentences.zh: 而且速度很快。

sentences.en: You could hop in, grab a custom-made quinoa bowl, and then go back to work without even pausing your podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以快进快出，拿上一份定制的藜麦碗，然后回到工作岗位，甚至都不用暂停你的播客。

sentences.en: And I hated it so much.
sentences.zh: 但我非常讨厌它。

sentences.en: As soon as I heard about Itza, I was like, okay, great.
sentences.zh: 我一听说Itza，我就想，好吧，太棒了。

sentences.en: Just what we need.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们所需要的。

sentences.en: To be even more removed from our food.
sentences.zh: 让我们离食物更远一点。

sentences.en: Not only where it comes from, but also the person who hands it to you.
sentences.zh: 不仅是离食物的来源更远，也离那个递给你食物的人更远。

sentences.en: Because it's not like it's a completely robot restaurant.
sentences.zh: 因为它并不是一家完全的机器人餐馆。

sentences.en: There's still people back there, behind the cubbies, slicing your avocados.
sentences.zh: 储物格后面依然有人在为你切牛油果。

sentences.en: They're just conveniently placed out of sight so that you don't have to say thank you.
sentences.zh: 他们只是被刻意安置在视线之外，这样你就不必说谢谢了。

sentences.en: Like, ah!
sentences.zh: 就像是，啊！

sentences.en: But you never actually tried it.
sentences.zh: 但你从来没试过。

sentences.en: Okay, no.
sentences.zh: 好吧，没有。

sentences.en: I never went there.
sentences.zh: 我从来没去过那里。

sentences.en: So take it with a big, fat pinch of salt.
sentences.zh: 所以，听听就好，别太当真。

sentences.en: And also, know that I hated it because it was very fun to hate.
sentences.zh: 而且要知道，我讨厌它是因为讨厌它本身就很有趣。

sentences.en: It was like juicers that connect to your phone with Bluetooth.
sentences.zh: 就像那些通过蓝牙连接手机的榨汁机一样。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你懂吗？

sentences.en: Just like stuff that is so completely lampoonably San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 就是那种非常具有旧金山特色的、完全可以被嘲讽的东西。

sentences.en: And so I did what I always do when I'm upset about a stupid thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了我一贯的做法，每当我因为一件蠢事感到心烦时。

sentences.en: I tweeted about it.
sentences.zh: 我在推特上吐槽了它。

sentences.en: And instead of getting in a fight, a number of people on Twitter pointed out that this restaurant
sentences.zh: 结果推特上很多人没有跟我吵架，而是指出这家餐馆

sentences.en: is not a distinctly modern phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 并不是什么现代特有的现象。

sentences.en: Something very similar existed at the turn of the century, over 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 早在世纪之交，也就是100多年前，就存在非常类似的东西了。

sentences.en: And it was not a San Francisco thing.
sentences.zh: 而且那也不是旧金山的东西。

sentences.en: It was very New York.
sentences.zh: 那是地道的纽约风味。

sentences.en: I grew up in this city.
sentences.zh: 我在这座城市长大。

sentences.en: And the city that I grew up in, and the city I'm living in now, ain't never met each other.
sentences.zh: 我长大的那座城市，和我现在居住的这座城市，简直是两个世界。

sentences.en: This is one of the New Yorkiest people I have ever met.
sentences.zh: 这是我见过最有“纽约味”的人之一。

sentences.en: Lorraine Deal.
sentences.zh: 洛林·迪尔。

sentences.en: Well, I write about New York history, so I'm always fishing around for something that I want to write about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我写关于纽约历史的文章，所以我总是在寻找我想写的东西。

sentences.en: My grandmother lived on 42nd Street and 8th Avenue.
sentences.zh: 我祖母住在第42街和第8大道交汇处。

sentences.en: I used to meet her under the clock of the Franklin Savings Bank on Saturday afternoons.
sentences.zh: 我过去常在周六下午和她在富兰克林储蓄银行的钟下见面。

sentences.en: We would go to Horn and Hardart.
sentences.zh: 我们会去霍恩与哈达特餐馆。

sentences.en: Ask anyone who was a kid in New York in the 50s or 60s.
sentences.zh: 问问任何在50或60年代在纽约长大的孩子。

sentences.en: They went to Horn and Hardart.
sentences.zh: 他们都去过霍恩与哈达特。

sentences.en: It was a popular restaurant chain that was, in many ways, the Itza of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 那是一家很受欢迎的连锁餐厅，在很多方面，它就是20世纪的Itza。

sentences.en: It had locations all over New York City and Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 它在纽约市和费城到处都有分店。

sentences.en: And it had very solid, standard fare.
sentences.zh: 而且它提供非常扎实、标准的餐点。

sentences.en: We're talking literal meat and potatoes.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是实打实的肉和土豆。

sentences.en: What was your favorite dish?
sentences.zh: 你最喜欢的菜是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, it was Salisbury steak and mashed potatoes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是索尔兹伯里牛排配土豆泥。

sentences.en: And when Lorraine decided that she wanted to write about Horn and Hardart, she got connected with Marianne.
sentences.zh: 当洛林决定写关于霍恩与哈达特的故事时，她联系上了玛丽安。

sentences.en: People don't always connect my last name with Horn and Hardart, but when they do, immediately stories start to come.
sentences.zh: 人们并不总是把我的姓氏和霍恩与哈达特联系起来，但当他们联系起来时，故事就会源源不断地涌现。

sentences.en: Marianne Hardart is the great-granddaughter of Horn and Hardart co-founder Frank Hardart.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安·哈达特是霍恩与哈达特联合创始人弗兰克·哈达特的曾孙女。

sentences.en: Together, Marianne Hardart and Lorraine Deal teamed up to write the definitive history of this restaurant chain.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安·哈达特和洛林·迪尔联手写下了这家连锁餐厅的权威历史。

sentences.en: Turns out these two live near each other on the Upper East Side, and they get along like a house on fire.
sentences.zh: 结果这两个人住在上东区附近，而且她们相处得非常融洽。

sentences.en: We didn't step on each other's toes.
sentences.zh: 我们从不互相妨碍。

sentences.en: At all.
sentences.zh: 一点也没有。

sentences.en: At all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: But Horn and Hardart restaurants also went by another name, a much more famous name, the Automat.
sentences.zh: 但霍恩与哈达特餐馆还有一个名字，一个更出名的名字，叫“自动餐馆”。

sentences.en: So what's the Automat?
sentences.zh: 那么什么是自动餐馆？

sentences.en: So it was the first time that you could go up to a wall, put money in, and get food, hot or cold.
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次可以走到墙边，投币，然后拿到热的或冷的食物。

sentences.en: Fresh prepared.
sentences.zh: 现做的。

sentences.en: Inside a Horn and Hardart Automat, it looked like a glamorous, ornate cafeteria.
sentences.zh: 在霍恩与哈达特的自动餐馆里，它看起来像是一个华丽、装饰精美的自助餐厅。

sentences.en: But instead of a human handing you hot food over a steaming counter, you'd push your tray up to a wall of little glass cubbies,
sentences.zh: 但你不是从冒着热气的柜台后接过食物，而是把托盘推到一堵小玻璃储物格墙前，

sentences.en: each housing a fresh, hot portion of food on a small plate.
sentences.zh: 每个格子里都放着一份新鲜热腾腾的食物，装在小盘子里。

sentences.en: Maybe it would be a side of peas.
sentences.zh: 可能是一份豌豆。

sentences.en: Maybe a turkey sandwich or a slice of pie.
sentences.zh: 也可能是一个火鸡三明治或一片派。

sentences.en: And you put in some nickels, and then the door to that cubby would unlock, and you could just take the plate that was inside.
sentences.zh: 你投进几个镍币，那个格子的门就会解锁，你就可以直接拿走里面的盘子。

sentences.en: That food was yours.
sentences.zh: 那份食物就是你的了。

sentences.en: This place where you could put money in a slot and pick your own food.
sentences.zh: 在这个地方，你可以把钱投进槽里，挑选自己的食物。

sentences.en: So for children, you know, the parents would give them some money, they would run up to the windows,
sentences.zh: 所以对于孩子们来说，你知道，父母会给他们一些钱，他们会跑向窗口，

sentences.en: they could pick what they wanted, they could put their nickel in and get their own food.
sentences.zh: 他们可以挑选自己想要的，投进镍币，拿到自己的食物。

sentences.en: It was really cheap.
sentences.zh: 它真的很便宜。

sentences.en: By the way, I hear the beef steak pie is a magnificent six nickels.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我听说牛肉派只要六个镍币，非常划算。

sentences.en: And it was pretty good.
sentences.zh: 而且味道相当不错。

sentences.en: Don't be a sucker, sister.
sentences.zh: 别当傻瓜，姐妹。

sentences.en: That beef pie is a wall.
sentences.zh: 那牛肉派简直硬得像块墙。

sentences.en: You see automats in a ton of movies, ranging from silent films like The Early Bird in 1925 to Witt Stillman's Metropolitan in 1990.
sentences.zh: 你在很多电影里都能看到自动餐馆，从1925年的默片《早起鸟》到1990年惠特·斯蒂尔曼的《大都会》。

sentences.en: I think I'll have a cake or two nickels.
sentences.zh: 我想我要个蛋糕，或者两个镍币的。

sentences.en: Yeah, wait a minute, wait a minute, wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 等等，等一下，等一下，等一下。

sentences.en: Seeing a character in an automat tells you they're a certain kind of American.
sentences.zh: 看到一个角色在自动餐馆里，就说明他们是某种特定的美国人。

sentences.en: One who wants to go out to eat, but doesn't have the budget.
sentences.zh: 那种想出去吃饭，但预算有限的人。

sentences.en: But my dear, she has no background.
sentences.zh: 但亲爱的，她没有背景。

sentences.en: Like in this short from 1932.
sentences.zh: 就像这部1932年的短片里一样。

sentences.en: One would hardly want to be seen dining out with her.
sentences.zh: 人们可不想和她一起出去吃饭。

sentences.en: It opens with a group of people in fancy hats, dining like royals.
sentences.zh: 开头是一群戴着华丽帽子的人，像皇室成员一样用餐。

sentences.en: I'd like another cup of coffee.
sentences.zh: 我想要再来一杯咖啡。

sentences.en: But then the camera zooms out and, womp, womp, they're in an automat.
sentences.zh: 但随后镜头拉远，砰，砰，他们是在自动餐馆里。

sentences.en: And this is also a punchline when Marilyn Monroe sings Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend.
sentences.zh: 当玛丽莲·梦露唱《钻石是女孩最好的朋友》时，这也是一个笑点。

sentences.en: But it won't pay the rental on your humble flat.
sentences.zh: 但这付不起你简陋公寓的租金。

sentences.en: Or help you at the automat.
sentences.zh: 也帮不了你在自动餐馆的开销。

sentences.en: And none of these movies explain what the automat is.
sentences.zh: 这些电影里都没有解释什么是自动餐馆。

sentences.en: It's just assumed that everyone knew.
sentences.zh: 大家都默认每个人都知道。

sentences.en: The Broadway columns in the newspapers are talking about who was seen at the automat.
sentences.zh: 报纸上的百老汇专栏都在谈论谁在自动餐馆被看到了。

sentences.en: Gene Kelly, when he was doing Pal Joey on Broadway, he and his wife would go over there.
sentences.zh: 吉恩·凯利在百老汇演《帕尔·乔伊》时，他和妻子就会去那里。

sentences.en: And Gregory Peck would love their scrambled eggs or something.
sentences.zh: 格里高利·派克也很喜欢他们的炒蛋之类的东西。

sentences.en: Counts and countesses coming in from Europe would say, we've got to try this.
sentences.zh: 从欧洲来的伯爵和伯爵夫人会说，我们一定要试试这个。

sentences.en: And they would sit down next to people who were flat broke.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会坐在身无分文的人旁边。

sentences.en: And you didn't have to tip?
sentences.zh: 而且你不需要付小费？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不需要。

sentences.en: Which is kind of like Itza.
sentences.zh: 这和Itza有点像。

sentences.en: And that was the automat 110 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这就是110年前的自动餐馆。

sentences.en: The story of the automat started when Joe Horn met Frank Hardart.
sentences.zh: 自动餐馆的故事始于乔·霍恩遇见弗兰克·哈达特。

sentences.en: Joe had put an ad in a local Philadelphia paper seeking a business partner.
sentences.zh: 乔在当地一份费城报纸上登了广告，寻找商业伙伴。

sentences.en: And so they got together and they opened a luncheonette in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 于是他们走到了一起，在费城开了一家午餐店。

sentences.en: Okay, over to you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，交给你了。

sentences.en: No, no, that's it.
sentences.zh: 不，不，就是这样。

sentences.en: Just adding a year.
sentences.zh: 只是加个年份。

sentences.en: And for a while it was just a normal luncheonette with famously good coffee.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，它只是一家普通的午餐店，以咖啡好喝而闻名。

sentences.en: Until Frank Hardart went over to Germany, right?
sentences.zh: 直到弗兰克·哈达特去了德国，对吧？

sentences.en: He was going to give himself a vacation.
sentences.zh: 他打算给自己放个假。

sentences.en: There, Hardart encountered some very early German vending machine technology.
sentences.zh: 在那里，哈达特接触到了一些非常早期的德国自动售货机技术。

sentences.en: Hardart bought one of these machines and brought it back to Philly.
sentences.zh: 哈达特买了一台这样的机器，把它带回了费城。

sentences.en: It was more Rube Goldberg contraption.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一个鲁布·戈德堡式的装置。

sentences.en: But no one knows who Rube Goldberg is.
sentences.zh: 但没人知道鲁布·戈德堡是谁。

sentences.en: I don't say that anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不再那样说了。

sentences.en: Do you know who Rube Goldberg is?
sentences.zh: 你知道鲁布·戈德堡是谁吗？

sentences.en: With this overly complicated German vending contraption, the food in the windows was a
sentences.zh: 有了这个过于复杂的德国自动售货装置，橱窗里的食物只是

sentences.en: sample display of what one could order.
sentences.zh: 人们可以点餐的样品展示。

sentences.en: Customers would deposit a coin and wait around while someone in the basement cooked it and
sentences.zh: 顾客投下一枚硬币，然后等着，同时地下室里有人把它做好，

sentences.en: then cranked it up in a dumbwaiter.
sentences.zh: 然后用升降机把它送上来。

sentences.en: It was a very convoluted way of getting your food, but everyone loved the novelty of it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常繁琐的取餐方式，但每个人都喜欢它的新奇感。

sentences.en: So they perfected it and then they brought it to New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以他们完善了它，然后把它带到了纽约市。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Went to New York City about 10 years later.
sentences.zh: 大约10年后去了纽约市。

sentences.en: 10 years later.
sentences.zh: 10年后。

sentences.en: So it was in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在费城。

sentences.en: The first automat was 1902 and then they came to New York City in 1912.
sentences.zh: 第一家自动餐馆是1902年开的，然后他们在1912年来到了纽约市。

sentences.en: And now, equipped with the glass cubbies, the automat caught on.
sentences.zh: 现在，配备了玻璃储物格，自动餐馆流行了起来。

sentences.en: FaSt.
sentences.zh: 很快。

sentences.en: But not because of the technology.
sentences.zh: 但不是因为技术。

sentences.en: That was just to get people in the door.
sentences.zh: 那只是为了吸引人们进门。

sentences.en: The automat part was just this glorious gimmick.
sentences.zh: 自动餐馆的部分只是一个辉煌的噱头。

sentences.en: People came for the novelty, but came back again and again because it was solid, good food
sentences.zh: 人们因为新奇而来，但一次又一次地回来，是因为它有扎实、美味的食物。

sentences.en: and cheap.
sentences.zh: 而且很便宜。

sentences.en: The technology was just a mechanical Turk.
sentences.zh: 这项技术其实只是个“土耳其机器人”（机械骗局）。

sentences.en: The only thing that was automatic was when you went in there and looked at this wall,
sentences.zh: 唯一自动化的部分，就是当你走进去看着那面墙时，

sentences.en: but what was going on behind those walls is very different.
sentences.zh: 但墙后发生的事情却大不相同。

sentences.en: Behind the scenes, there were people scurrying around, replacing all the food.
sentences.zh: 在幕后，有工人们忙碌地穿梭，不断更换所有的食物。

sentences.en: Past the vending walls were scores of workers, many of whom were recent immigrants, rapidly
sentences.zh: 自动售货墙后有许多工人，其中许多是刚来的移民，他们迅速地

sentences.en: replenishing the food into the cubbies and darting out to bust and clean dishware.
sentences.zh: 将食物补充到小格子里，并跑进跑出地收拾和清洗餐具。

sentences.en: And as automats expanded to more locations in both Philadelphia and New York, all the
sentences.zh: 随着自动售货餐厅（Automat）在费城和纽约开设更多分店，所有的

sentences.en: cooking itself happened in off-site commissaries.
sentences.zh: 烹饪工作都在场外的中央厨房完成。

sentences.zh: 这些是独立的厨房，占据了整整一个街区。

sentences.en: But their PR representative told me that now Itza is focused on selling their serving technology to other chains,
sentences.zh: 但他们的公关代表告诉我，现在 Itza 专注于向其他连锁店销售他们的服务技术，

sentences.en: like a macaroni and cheese restaurant called Mact,
sentences.zh: 比如一家叫 Mact 的通心粉奶酪餐厅，

sentences.en: and another chain called WowBow.
sentences.zh: 以及另一家叫 WowBow 的连锁店。

sentences.en: Even at McDonald's, it's pretty common to order on a screen.
sentences.zh: 即使在麦当劳，通过屏幕点餐也已经非常普遍了。

sentences.en: And a salad-making robot named Sally is being put in a restaurant chain based in Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama.
sentences.zh: 而且，一台名为“莎莉”的沙拉制作机器人正在被引入路易斯安那州、密西西比州和阿拉巴马州的连锁餐厅。

sentences.en: There are new iterations of vending machines and faceless delivery and robot chefs popping up everywhere.
sentences.zh: 各种自动售货机、无人配送和机器人厨师的新迭代产品正层出不穷。

sentences.en: The point is, yes, horn and hard art restaurants are gone.
sentences.zh: 重点是，没错，霍恩和哈达特餐厅已经消失了。

sentences.en: But more and more chains are becoming automats.
sentences.zh: 但越来越多的连锁店正在变成自动餐厅。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Roe Flagg, David Bordeaux, and Imuna Hauser, and Ira Goldman.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢 Roe Flagg、David Bordeaux、Imuna Hauser 和 Ira Goldman。

sentences.en: You can find out more about Lisa Hurwitz' documentary and share your automat memories at facebook.com slash theautomatthemovie.
sentences.zh: 你可以访问 facebook.com/theautomatthemovie 了解更多关于 Lisa Hurwitz 的纪录片，并分享你对自动餐厅的记忆。

sentences.en: Coming up, robots that throw food, all in an effort to make that food seem more delicious.
sentences.zh: 接下来，会抛掷食物的机器人，这一切都是为了让食物看起来更美味。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后见。

sentences.en: When we were editing this story about the automat, it brought to mind another story about robots and food that we did a couple years back
sentences.zh: 当我们剪辑这期关于自动餐厅的故事时，我想起了几年前我们做的另一个关于机器人和食物的故事，

sentences.en: that I love because it may be the most perfect example of the 99% invisible effort
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢那个故事，因为它可能是“99% 无形努力”最完美的例证，

sentences.en: that goes into something that most people do not think about at all.
sentences.zh: 这种努力投入到了大多数人根本不会去想的事情中。

sentences.en: But it totally changed the way we buy and consume food.
sentences.zh: 但它彻底改变了我们购买和消费食物的方式。

sentences.en: Check it out.
sentences.zh: 来看看吧。

sentences.en: Of all the ads you see on TV or on billboards or on the sides of buses, an overwhelming number seem to be for food.
sentences.zh: 在你电视、广告牌或公交车身上看到的所有广告中，绝大多数似乎都是关于食物的。

sentences.en: This is our masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的杰作。

sentences.en: Boar's head oven gold turkey.
sentences.zh: Boar's Head 烤箱金火鸡。

sentences.en: Eggs and sausage.
sentences.zh: 鸡蛋和香肠。

sentences.en: Hot cakes and butter.
sentences.zh: 热蛋糕和黄油。

sentences.en: I see Cokes in frosted glasses.
sentences.zh: 我看到了冰镇玻璃杯里的可乐。

sentences.en: Fajitas sizzling on the grill.
sentences.zh: 烤架上滋滋作响的法士达。

sentences.en: Well, at Longhorn, what's in season matters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在 Longhorn，当季食材很重要。

sentences.en: A guy biting into the perfect hamburger on a sesame seed bun.
sentences.zh: 一个人咬下一口芝麻面包里完美的汉堡。

sentences.en: Peak ingredients.
sentences.zh: 顶级食材。

sentences.en: Perfectly cooked.
sentences.zh: 烹饪得恰到好处。

sentences.en: But of course, you know, in real life, these foods don't look like they do in the ads.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你知道，在现实生活中，这些食物看起来和广告里不一样。

sentences.en: I'm here with a question from Isabel M.
sentences.zh: 我这里有一个来自安大略省多伦多的 Isabel M. 的问题。

sentences.en: from Toronto, Ontario.
sentences.zh: 她问，为什么你们的食物在广告里看起来和店里卖的不一样？

sentences.en: She asks, why does your food look different in the advertising than what's in the store?
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，Isabel。

sentences.en: It's a great question, Isabel.
sentences.zh: 我们经常被问到这个问题。

sentences.en: We get asked that a lot.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意跟我来，我要带你穿过马路。

sentences.en: And if you want to come with me, I'm going to take you across the street.
sentences.zh: 我们要去一探究竟。

sentences.en: We're going to find out a bit more.
sentences.zh: 来吧。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 2012 年，麦当劳加拿大公司发布了这段关于他们拍摄汉堡过程的视频。

sentences.en: In 2012, McDonald's Canada put out this video about the process they go through to photograph one of their burgers.
sentences.zh: 我现在要向大家介绍我们的食物造型师 Noah。

sentences.en: What I'm going to do is introduce you now to Noah, who's our food styliSt.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我认为有必要说明一下，Noah 使用的所有食材都和我们在餐厅里使用的是完全一样的。

sentences.en: And here, I think it's important to note that all the ingredients that Noah uses are the exact same ingredients that we use in the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 视频记录了食物造型师 Noah 如何精心挑选最完美的洋葱片和酸黄瓜片。

sentences.en: The video follows food stylist Noah as he painstakingly selects the perfect slices of onion and pickle.
sentences.zh: 他用镊子把它们放在汉堡上，然后精准地将奶酪融化到恰到好处。

sentences.en: He places them on the burger with tweezers and then precisely melts the cheese just so.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能用调色刀把奶酪融化掉。

sentences.en: I hope I'm just melting down the cheese with my palette knife.
sentences.zh: 然后他拿起一个装满番茄酱的塑料注射器，以手术般的精度涂抹上去。

sentences.en: Then he picks up a plastic syringe filled with ketchup and applies it with surgical precision.
sentences.zh: 也许我该放点芥末、番茄酱，其实是番茄酱、芥末、番茄酱。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll put mustard, ketchup, actually ketchup, mustard, ketchup.
sentences.zh: 然后他们拍摄这个精美的汉堡，并用 Photoshop 将其修饰到完美。

sentences.en: Then they photograph this fancy burger and Photoshop it to perfection.
sentences.zh: 真不错。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 他们把一张刚在麦当劳点好的真实汉堡照片放在这个造型汉堡的图片旁边。

sentences.en: They place a picture of a real burger just ordered at McDonald's next to the image of this stylized burger.
sentences.zh: 对比非常强烈。

sentences.en: And the difference is striking.
sentences.zh: 那是记者 Danny Lewis。

sentences.en: That's reporter Danny Lewis.
sentences.zh: 我想吃 Noah 造型和拆解的那个汉堡。

sentences.en: I would like to eat the burger that Noah styled and dissembled.
sentences.zh: 另一个嘛，就不太想吃了。

sentences.en: The other one, not so much.
sentences.zh: 过去一百年左右的食品广告都是由一个简单的事实塑造的。

sentences.en: The last hundred years or so of food advertising have been shaped by this one simple fact.
sentences.zh: 真实的食物在镜头下看起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: Real food looks bad on camera.
sentences.zh: 在广告中拍摄食物，甚至只是给食物拍照，一直都难得要命。

sentences.en: Shooting food and even photographing food has always been fiendishly difficult in advertising.
sentences.zh: 这是 Terry O'Reilly。

sentences.en: This is Terry O'Reilly.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他一直是一名广告人，现在他主持一档关于广告的广播节目，叫《潜移默化》(Under the Influence)。

sentences.en: For decades, he was an ad man and he now hosts a radio show about advertising called Under the Influence.
sentences.zh: Terry 说，拍摄食物的挑战显而易见。

sentences.en: Terry says the challenges of shooting food are obvious.
sentences.zh: 首先，食物放在盘子里不动的时候看起来很无聊。

sentences.en: First of all, food is boring to look at when it's just sitting on a plate.
sentences.zh: 因为食物通常是静态的。

sentences.en: Because food is generally static.
sentences.zh: 当你把它放在摄影棚的热灯光下时，

sentences.en: Then when you subject it to the hot lights of a studio.
sentences.zh: 食物就开始枯萎了。

sentences.en: The food starts to wilt.
sentences.zh: 这只是简单的科学原理。

sentences.en: It's just simple science.
sentences.zh: 因此，广告商必须不断在“美化”和“造假”之间走钢丝。

sentences.en: And so advertisers have had to constantly walk this fine line between enhancement and fakery.
sentences.zh: 尝试各种技巧让食物看起来诱人。

sentences.en: Trying all kinds of tricks to get food to look good.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪的前半叶，甚至在摄影技术被广泛采用很久之后，杂志和报纸上的广告商仍然非常依赖插画。

sentences.en: For the first half of the 20th century, well after photography was widely adopted, advertisers in magazines and newspapers relied heavily on illustration.
sentences.zh: 插画之所以成为首选方法，是因为你可以完全控制插画。

sentences.en: The reason illustration was the preferred method was because you could completely control an illustration.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，没有灯光问题。

sentences.en: In other words, there's no lighting issues.
sentences.zh: 没有食物枯萎的问题。

sentences.en: There's no wilting food issues.
sentences.zh: 营销人员真的可以完全决定食物的样子，甚至精确到每一根意大利面，只要有插画师在场。

sentences.en: A marketer could really completely dictate what that food would look like right down to the strand of pasta with an illustrator.
sentences.zh: 后来，电视在 20 世纪 50 年代和 60 年代出现了。

sentences.en: Then TV came along in the 1950s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 广告商面临着一系列全新的挑战。

sentences.en: And advertisers faced a whole new set of challenges.
sentences.zh: 我要向你们展示麦当劳是如何制作巨无霸三明治的。

sentences.en: I'm going to show you how McDonald's builds a Big Mac sandwich.
sentences.zh: 很多人并不真正懂得如何以引人注目的方式拍摄食物。

sentences.en: A lot of them didn't really understand how to shoot food in a compelling way.
sentences.zh: 在这个广告中，汉堡只是放在柜台上，而食材被堆叠上去。

sentences.en: In this ad, the hamburger just sits there on the counter while the ingredients get piled on.
sentences.zh: 从这里开始，放上一片轻微烤过的面包。

sentences.en: It starts here with a lightly toasted bun.
sentences.zh: 然后是一块纯牛肉汉堡肉饼。

sentences.en: And then a pure beef hamburger.
sentences.zh: 滋滋作响，热气腾腾。

sentences.en: Sizzling hot.
sentences.zh: 如果没有引人注目的视觉效果，通常会有画外音对食物进行极尽描述。

sentences.en: Without compelling visuals, there'd often be a voiceover just describing the hell out of the food.
sentences.zh: 列出食材，告诉你它有多好吃。

sentences.en: Listing ingredients, telling you how good it tasted.
sentences.zh: 再加点酱汁，味道更好。

sentences.en: And a little more sauce just for good flavor.
sentences.zh: 爽脆的莳萝酸黄瓜。

sentences.en: Crisp dill pickles.
sentences.zh: 还有芝麻面包顶盖。

sentences.en: And the sesame seed crown.
sentences.zh: 这些早期的电视广告依赖于相对静态的镜头。

sentences.en: These early TV ads relied on relatively static shots.
sentences.zh: 广告商会在摄像机上安装广角镜头。

sentences.en: Advertisers would use a wide-angle lens mounted on a camera.
sentences.zh: 可能会放大并平移一点，但仅此而已。

sentences.en: And it might zoom in and pan a little, but that's about it.
sentences.zh: 有很多盒子和标签的镜头。

sentences.en: There were lots of shots of boxes and labels.
sentences.zh: 食物只是在做正常的食物该做的事。

sentences.en: The food did just normal food stuff.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到东西从锅里舀出来。

sentences.en: You might see something being ladled out of a pot.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到，你知道，餐桌上有人用勺子盛豌豆或盛奶油玉米。

sentences.en: You might see, you know, a spoon serving peas at a dinner table or serving cream corn at a dinner table.
sentences.zh: 这就是动作的极限了。

sentences.en: So that would be the extent of the motion.
sentences.zh: 除了电视带来的新挑战，60 年代末的食品广告商还发现自己面临着新的审查。

sentences.en: On top of the new challenges of television, food advertisers in the late 60s found themselves facing new scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 在 1968 年臭名昭著的“金宝汤事件”之后，联邦贸易委员会一直在密切关注电视广告。

sentences.en: The Federal Trade Commission was keeping a close eye on TV ads following the now infamous Campbell's Soup Incident of 1968.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在推出一个新品牌的汤，里面有很多蔬菜，但问题是蔬菜会沉到底部。

sentences.en: They were introducing a new brand of soup that had a lot of vegetables in it, but the problem is the vegetables sink to the bottom.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做的是在碗底放了一堆弹珠，只是为了把蔬菜托起来。

sentences.en: So what they did was put a bunch of marbles in the bottom of the bowls just to hoist up the vegetables.
sentences.zh: 当联邦贸易委员会发现后，他们威胁要对金宝汤公司采取法律行动。

sentences.en: When the FTC found out, they threatened Campbell's with legal action.
sentences.zh: 这一事件推动了广告界对“真实性”的追求。

sentences.en: The event led to a new push for truth in advertising.
sentences.zh: 广告商过去依赖的许多老把戏现在都行不通了。

sentences.en: A lot of the old tricks advertisers had relied on in the past were now off the table.
sentences.zh: 麦片广告里不能再用胶水代替牛奶了。

sentences.en: No more using glue instead of milk in cereal ads.
sentences.zh: 不能再用土豆泥代替冰淇淋了。

sentences.en: No more substituting mashed potatoes for ice cream.
sentences.zh: 但在 20 世纪 70 年代，食品广告发生了彻底的转变。

sentences.en: But in the 1970s, food advertising took a radical turn.
sentences.zh: 食物开始动起来了。

sentences.en: Food started moving.
sentences.zh: 这为我们今天在广告中看到的各种花哨技巧打开了大门。

sentences.en: And that opened the door to all the fancy tricks we see in ads today.
sentences.zh: 虾在做杂技翻转。

sentences.en: Shrimp executing acrobatic flips.
sentences.zh: 龙虾钳在慢动作中裂开。

sentences.en: Lobster claws cracking open in slow motion.
sentences.zh: 炸薯条在桌子上跳跃。

sentences.en: French fries bouncing across a table.
sentences.zh: 食物不再是静态的了。

sentences.en: Food wasn't static anymore.
sentences.zh: 食物飞了起来。

sentences.en: Food was flying.
sentences.zh: 我们要感谢一个人带来了这种新的美学。

sentences.en: And we've got one man to thank for this new aesthetic.
sentences.zh: 我们要感谢一个人带来了这种新美学。

sentences.en: Elbert Buden.
sentences.zh: 他不想要任何停滞的东西。

sentences.en: He didn't want anything stagnant.
sentences.zh: 一切都在不断运动。

sentences.en: Everything was always moving.
sentences.zh: 他想让食物或他面前的任何东西充满浪漫色彩。

sentences.en: He wanted to romance the food or whatever was there in front of him.
sentences.zh: 这是 Harry Drennan，他曾为 Elbert Buden 工作多年。

sentences.en: This is Harry Drennan, who spent years working for Elbert Buden.
sentences.zh: 他就是在那儿遇到了他的妻子，布景导演 Jackie Canto。

sentences.en: That's how he met his wife, set director Jackie Canto.
sentences.zh: 我在电影行业干了 35 年，40 年了。

sentences.en: I've been in the film business for 35 years, 40.
sentences.zh: 我不想说具体多久。

sentences.en: I don't want to say how long.
sentences.zh: Canto 和 Drennan 在 1996 年 Buden 去世前与他合作制作的广告是史无前例的。

sentences.en: The ads that Canto and Drennan made with Buden until his death in 1996 were unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 与麦当劳、汉堡王和可口可乐等客户合作，

sentences.en: Working with clients like McDonald's, Burger King, and Coca-Cola,
sentences.zh: Buden 为食品广告发明了一种全新的视觉语言，

sentences.en: Buden invented a whole new visual language for food commercials
sentences.zh: 并真正开创了被称为“桌面摄影”的广告流派。

sentences.en: and really pioneered the genre of advertising known as tabletop.
sentences.zh: 许多桌面摄影导演至今仍在使用的术语和技术都可以追溯到 Buden。

sentences.en: Many of the terms and techniques that tabletop directors still use date back to Buden.
sentences.zh: 例如，“准备镜头”，它讲述了产品的背景故事，

sentences.en: For example, the prep shot, which tells the backstory of the product,
sentences.zh: 展示了制作食物所投入的一切。

sentences.en: showing all that goes into making the food.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那些切碎爽脆的生菜、切丁多汁的红番茄的镜头。

sentences.en: You know, the ones, chopping a crisp head of lettuce, dicing some juicy red tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 他会把原材料摆成精致的宴席，这就是他的风格。

sentences.en: He would make these elaborate banquet things of raw ingredients, and that was his look.
sentences.zh: 还有“渴望镜头”。

sentences.en: And crave shots.
sentences.zh: 那是摄像机极度放大，停留在叉子上那一口诱人的食物上。

sentences.en: That's when the camera zooms way in and lingers on some tantalizing bite of food on the end of a fork.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上很性感，你知道，这几乎是“食物色情”，你懂的。

sentences.en: Sexy in a way, you know, it's almost food porn, you know.
sentences.zh: 它让你感觉一切都触手可及。

sentences.en: It's made it all real tactile to you.
sentences.zh: 还有“英雄镜头”。

sentences.en: And the hero shot.
sentences.zh: 最后一次壮观地展示盘子里的食物，准备好享用。

sentences.en: A last magnificent look at the food, on the plate, ready to eat.
sentences.zh: 通常在广告的最后几秒钟出现。

sentences.en: Usually in the final seconds of the advertisement.
sentences.zh: Buden 的重大突破在于，他不仅仅是描述食物并向观众承诺它很好吃。

sentences.en: Buden's big breakthrough was that he didn't just describe the food and promise viewers it tasted good.
sentences.zh: 他用他的画面让观众感受到了真实的饥饿感。

sentences.en: He made them feel actual hunger with his images.
sentences.zh: 他真正厉害的地方在于食物本身，它的本质，确实非常感性。

sentences.en: His real thing is just food in itself, its essence, is really sensual.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一个汉堡广告，你真的会想吃一个汉堡。

sentences.en: If you see a hamburger commercial, you really want to eat a hamburger.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一个汉堡广告，你真的会想吃一个汉堡。

sentences.en: And that's the point of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是重点所在。

sentences.en: And I think that's what he introduced.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是他所引入的东西。

sentences.en: And you'll never see it any other way now.
sentences.zh: 现在你再也不会以其他方式看待它了。

sentences.en: Canto and Drennan remember working long days, and sometimes long nights, to meet Buden's high standards.
sentences.zh: Canto 和 Drennan 记得为了达到 Buden 的高标准，他们经常工作很长时间，有时甚至通宵达旦。

sentences.en: And to achieve his vision of flying food and mouth-watering close-ups,
sentences.zh: 为了实现他脑海中食物飞舞和令人垂涎的特写镜头，

sentences.en: they had to use a whole bunch of crazy tools.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不使用一大堆疯狂的工具。

sentences.en: Like giant high-speed cameras that would burn through a thousand feet of film in seconds.
sentences.zh: 比如巨大的高速摄像机，几秒钟就能烧掉一千英尺的胶片。

sentences.en: They'd make a ton of noise.
sentences.zh: 它们会发出巨大的噪音。

sentences.en: They'd start shooting, and it was like,
sentences.zh: 一旦开始拍摄，就像是，

sentences.en: It was just this, all day long.
sentences.zh: 整整一天都是这样。

sentences.en: It was something.
sentences.zh: 那真是一回事。

sentences.en: These cameras were originally designed for the military to film rocket tests.
sentences.zh: 这些摄像机最初是为军方设计，用于拍摄火箭测试的。

sentences.en: It was used for ballistics, but we were the first ones to do it with food.
sentences.zh: 它原本用于弹道学，但我们是第一批用它来拍摄食物的人。

sentences.en: Thanks to these cameras, Buden could achieve super slow motion effects.
sentences.zh: 多亏了这些摄像机，Buden 才能实现超慢动作特效。

sentences.en: He'd take a split second of time and luxuriate in it.
sentences.zh: 他能截取极短的一瞬间，并尽情地展现它。

sentences.en: He'd have oranges splash through a sheet of water.
sentences.zh: 他会让橙子穿过水幕飞溅而出。

sentences.en: Condensation would drip down the side of a bottle.
sentences.zh: 冷凝水会顺着瓶身滴落。

sentences.en: In order to get the perfect take, Buden started designing strange Rube Goldberg sort of machines to help him get the job done.
sentences.zh: 为了拍出完美的镜头，Buden 开始设计各种奇怪的鲁布·戈德堡式机器来帮助他完成工作。

sentences.en: These contraptions were called rigs.
sentences.zh: 这些装置被称为“索具”。

sentences.en: They ranged from simple spouts for liquid, to machines that would drop pancakes into a perfect stack,
sentences.zh: 它们种类繁多，从简单的液体喷嘴，到能把煎饼叠成完美一摞的机器，

sentences.en: to catapults that would fling oranges across the studio.
sentences.zh: 再到能把橙子甩过摄影棚的弹射器。

sentences.en: And sure, the production team could have just thrown the oranges by hand.
sentences.zh: 当然，制作团队本可以只用手扔橙子。

sentences.en: But with a rig, they could get the exact same results over and over,
sentences.zh: 但有了这些装置，他们可以反复获得完全相同的结果，

sentences.en: which meant fewer takes, which meant less time and less money spent.
sentences.zh: 这意味着拍摄次数更少，花费的时间和金钱也更少。

sentences.en: It also meant that they could achieve a certain level of precision and artistry.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着他们可以达到一定的精确度和艺术水准。

sentences.en: It was so much prettier than other people's work, as far as I could see.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这比其他人的作品漂亮多了。

sentences.en: He was beautiful at lighting.
sentences.zh: 他在灯光运用上非常出色。

sentences.en: And then once he got into all the movement, I mean, he was ahead of the curve.
sentences.zh: 一旦涉及到动作设计，我的意思是，他走在了时代的前沿。

sentences.en: Lights roll, steam.
sentences.zh: 灯光准备，蒸汽准备。

sentences.en: Roll.
sentences.zh: 开始。

sentences.en: Out.
sentences.zh: 出去。

sentences.en: Ready?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗？

sentences.en: And action.
sentences.zh: 开始拍摄。

sentences.en: No, I missed it.
sentences.zh: 不，我错过了。

sentences.en: Try it again.
sentences.zh: 再试一次。

sentences.en: To see how Buden's techniques are still being used today, Danny went to MacGuffin Films in New York.
sentences.zh: 为了看看 Buden 的技术在今天是如何被使用的，Danny 去了纽约的 MacGuffin Films。

sentences.en: Okay, so just quick descriptions.
sentences.zh: 好的，简单描述一下。

sentences.en: MacGuffin does commercials for Red Lobster, Olive Garden, Starbucks, and a bunch of other restaurants.
sentences.zh: MacGuffin 为 Red Lobster、Olive Garden、Starbucks 以及其他许多餐厅制作广告。

sentences.en: The day Danny was there, they were shooting a chicken sandwich.
sentences.zh: Danny 在那儿的那天，他们正在拍摄一个鸡肉三明治。

sentences.en: So they are shooting a chicken sandwich, a hero shot, it looks like, on a black slate
sentences.zh: 他们正在拍摄一个鸡肉三明治，看起来是一个主打镜头，放在黑色石板上，

sentences.en: with a little tray of chili peppers and garlic and stuff.
sentences.zh: 旁边还有一小盘辣椒、大蒜之类的东西。

sentences.en: A hand model stands near the edge of the table where the sandwich is displayed.
sentences.zh: 一位手模站在展示三明治的桌子边缘附近。

sentences.en: So now they're doing the crowning.
sentences.zh: 现在他们正在进行“加冕”步骤。

sentences.en: Crowning means the hand model takes the bun and puts it on top of the sandwich.
sentences.zh: “加冕”是指手模拿起面包盖，把它放在三明治顶部。

sentences.en: Just presses it there, alluringly.
sentences.zh: 就这样诱人地按在那里。

sentences.en: Then takes the crown off.
sentences.zh: 然后把盖子拿走。

sentences.en: In between shots, a guy comes on with a fan brush to brush any of the chicken.
sentences.zh: 在拍摄间隙，一个人会拿着扇形刷来刷理鸡肉。

sentences.en: Then the crown goes back on again.
sentences.zh: 然后盖子又放回去了。

sentences.en: Would you mind just putting the crown back on that sandwich, please?
sentences.zh: 请问你能把盖子放回那个三明治上吗？

sentences.en: It took them all day to film this sandwich.
sentences.zh: 他们花了一整天时间才拍完这个三明治。

sentences.en: The whole shoot precisely orchestrated, relying on highly technical tools.
sentences.zh: 整个拍摄过程经过精心编排，依赖于高科技工具。

sentences.en: Downstairs in MacGuffin's prop room, there are all sorts of rigs sitting in storage, a lot
sentences.zh: 在 MacGuffin 的道具室楼下，存放着各种各样的装置，很多

sentences.en: like the ones that Buden developed.
sentences.zh: 都像 Buden 开发的那样。

sentences.en: But these are way more high-tech.
sentences.zh: 但这些要高科技得多。

sentences.en: Riggers today use lasers and sensors and pre-programmed motors.
sentences.zh: 现在的索具师使用激光、传感器和预编程电机。

sentences.en: And depending on the shot or the rig, there can be some intense physics to take into account.
sentences.zh: 根据拍摄内容或装置的不同，可能需要考虑一些复杂的物理学问题。

sentences.en: Like if you're trying to slice an onion in two while it's flying through the air.
sentences.zh: 比如如果你想在洋葱飞过空中时把它切成两半。

sentences.en: We break down the elements.
sentences.zh: 我们分解这些元素。

sentences.en: So we know we've got to get an onion to a certain height.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道必须让洋葱达到一定的高度。

sentences.en: This is Anthony DeRoberts.
sentences.zh: 这位是 Anthony DeRoberts。

sentences.en: He's a special effects technician at MacGuffin FilMs.
sentences.zh: 他是 MacGuffin Films 的特效技术员。

sentences.en: And he designed a special rig just to get this shot.
sentences.zh: 他专门设计了一个特殊的装置来拍摄这个镜头。

sentences.en: Everything's computer-controlled.
sentences.zh: 一切都是电脑控制的。

sentences.en: So when the onion's in the right spot, these two sharp knives come through,
sentences.zh: 所以当洋葱到达正确位置时，这两把锋利的刀会穿过，

sentences.en: split the onion, and leave you with the slice down the middle.
sentences.zh: 把洋葱劈开，留下中间切开的一片。

sentences.en: And slices of onion artfully tumbling across a table.
sentences.zh: 还有洋葱片艺术地滚过桌面。

sentences.en: Classic prep shot.
sentences.zh: 经典的准备镜头。

sentences.en: But while Buden may have introduced rigs and action to tabletop,
sentences.zh: 虽然 Buden 可能将装置和动作引入了桌面摄影，

sentences.en: some directors, like MacGuffin's Nick Fugelstad,
sentences.zh: 但一些导演，比如 MacGuffin 的 Nick Fugelstad，

sentences.en: are trying to get away from Buden's fantastical dreamscapes of flying shrimp and oranges.
sentences.zh: 正试图摆脱 Buden 那种充满飞舞虾仁和橙子的梦幻场景。

sentences.en: I think that's a little bit of an older point of view.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一个稍微过时的观点。

sentences.en: For Nick Fugelstad, the idealized images of food that Buden tried to bring to his ads
sentences.zh: 对于 Nick Fugelstad 来说，Buden 试图带入广告中的那种理想化食物图像，

sentences.en: just don't cut it in a world that's now totally saturated with food porn.
sentences.zh: 在如今这个充斥着“食物色情”的世界里已经行不通了。

sentences.en: While Buden's commercials often zoomed in so close to food that you couldn't see the space around it,
sentences.zh: Buden 的广告经常把镜头拉得离食物非常近，以至于你看不到周围的空间，

sentences.en: tabletop directors like Fugelstad now framed their food in a space that you might see out in the world,
sentences.zh: 而像 Fugelstad 这样的桌面导演现在把食物放在你可能在现实世界中看到的空间里，

sentences.en: like at a restaurant or a barbecue.
sentences.zh: 比如在餐厅或烧烤店。

sentences.en: You know, when you dig into a lasagna, do you want the sauce to go all over the place?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你吃千层面时，你希望酱汁到处都是吗？

sentences.en: We need a taco.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个塔可饼。

sentences.en: Is stuff going to fall out?
sentences.zh: 东西会掉出来吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so let's shoot that.
sentences.zh: 是的，那我们就拍那个。

sentences.en: You know, let the flavors mix.
sentences.zh: 你知道，让味道融合在一起。

sentences.en: It's all right.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: It's what tastes good.
sentences.zh: 那才是好吃的味道。

sentences.en: But the thing to remember is this.
sentences.zh: 但要记住这一点。

sentences.en: On the set of a food commercial, everything, everything is highly orchestrated and contrived,
sentences.zh: 在食物广告的片场，一切，一切都是高度编排和刻意设计的，

sentences.en: even if the ultimate effect feels somewhat natural.
sentences.zh: 即使最终的效果感觉很自然。

sentences.en: Because a 30-second TV spot by a firm like MacGuffin can cost literally hundreds of thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 因为像 MacGuffin 这样的公司制作一个 30 秒的电视广告，成本可能高达数十万美元。

sentences.en: So it's got to do one thing to make it all worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 所以它必须做一件事来让这一切物有所值。

sentences.en: Sell a lot of food.
sentences.zh: 卖出大量的食物。

sentences.en: I would say the number one rule in food advertising is that the first taste is always with the eyes.
sentences.zh: 我会说食物广告的第一法则就是：第一口总是先用眼睛吃的。

sentences.en: So you're trying to create a shot that makes somebody salivate.
sentences.zh: 所以你要尝试创造一个让人垂涎欲滴的镜头。

sentences.en: This is Terry O'Reilly again, and he's fascinated by the lengths people go to sell something.
sentences.zh: 这是 Terry O'Reilly，他很着迷于人们为了推销产品所付出的努力。

sentences.en: He tells a story about working on a commercial for a hamburger company
sentences.zh: 他讲了一个故事，关于他在为一家汉堡公司制作广告时，

sentences.en: and watching an actor do take after take, biting into a hamburger,
sentences.zh: 看着演员一遍又一遍地拍摄咬汉堡的镜头，

sentences.en: and then gazing into the camera with a look of total satisfaction on his face.
sentences.zh: 然后带着一脸完全满足的表情凝视镜头。

sentences.en: Then you cut, and then there's the spit pail right beside the actor,
sentences.zh: 然后导演喊停，演员旁边就有一个吐物桶，

sentences.en: and then they just spit it right into the pail.
sentences.zh: 他们直接把汉堡吐进桶里。

sentences.en: You know, cut.
sentences.zh: 你知道，喊停。

sentences.en: And you watch that happen 40 times or 30 times or 20 times.
sentences.zh: 你看着这一幕发生了 40 次、30 次或 20 次。

sentences.en: And it's so hilarious to me, just the mechanics of advertising.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说太搞笑了，这就是广告的运作机制。

sentences.en: The illusion and the reality of creating it.
sentences.zh: 创造它的幻觉与现实。

sentences.en: That's exactly it in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，就是这样。
